Theme

Latin word

dēdūcō

dēdūcō, dēdūcere, dēdūxī, dēductum

verb, third conjugation, transitive

escort (someone from his house); take (a young man) to a teacher or a patron; launch (a ship), draw down into the water; deduct

In this lexicon

  • accompany

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 63: dēdūcī, redūcī; Cic. Fam. 10.12.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • introduce

    also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 1: ā patre ita eram dēductus ad Scaevolam

  • launch

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 5.2.2: quīn paucīs diēbus dēdūcī possint; Verg. A. 4.398: nāvēs lītore dēdūcunt (Lewis & Short)

  • subtract

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.59: addendō dēdūcendōque; Liv. 6.15.10: dē capite dēdūcite, quod ūsūrīs pernumerātum est

Examples

  • trahuntque siccās māchinae carīnās

    and the winches drag the dry hulls down to the seaHor. C. 1.4.2

    In the entry for launch

  • nāvēs … invēnit īnstrūctās neque multum abesse ab eō quīn paucīs diēbus dēdūcī possint

    he found the ships fitted out and nearly ready to be launched in a few daysCaes. BG 5.2.2
